text:
alex: Hey team — customer 'Team Krypton' (project: team-krypton-demo-42) just hit a hard 429 during a live hackathon demo. They're blocked and asking for a short uplift so the demo can finish.

alex: Quick repro info: they call /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings concurrently from their demo script. Spike to ~120 rps for ~10m, normally ~5 rps. Keys have been rotated earlier today.

alex: example error they pasted:
```
$ curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-demo-xxxxx" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","prompt":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","detail":"concurrency limit exceeded for free tier: 10 rps"}
```

maria: thanks — do we have the customer contact + billing email? also need approximate window they need uplift for (hours). any sign of key leakage?

alex: contact is claire@teamkrypton.io, demo runs for another ~3 hours and ends at 19:00 PT. keys rotated so not leaked. they just blast parallel requests for demos.

rate-limit-bot: ALERT: free-tier-concurrency-limit triggered for project team-krypton-demo-42. peak=120 rps, avg=42 rps (5m). rule_id=ft-concur-10.

eng-oncall: We can do a temporary burst override. Options: small (50 rps, 6h) or medium (100 rps, 3h). Recommendation: grant 50 rps for 6h + enable automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant to reduce token cost. Also enable prefix caching for sessions.

sam-sales: if we grant this, do we tie it to a sales touch? sounds like a good upsell. claire indicated they'll consider paid tier if demo succeeds. Can support provide a short-term free uplift and follow-up call?

billing: One-time free uplift is allowed but we require a short note on file and the customer's billing email. We'll flag their account for a sales follow-up. No invoice for this exception. We need support to create an internal 'burst_exception' entry with reason and approver.

maria: Claire confirmed she wants the uplift and agrees to a sales call. She provided billing email (billing@teamkrypton.io). Requesting: +50 rps for 6h starting now. Approver?

eng-oncall: I can approve the technical change. Please run the internal grant command: `grant-burst --project team-krypton-demo-42 --rps 50 --duration 6h --reason "hackathon demo" --approved-by eng-oncall`. After that, enable fallback policy to redwood-lite-1.4q for requests that exceed 2s latency.

maria: running now...

maria: `/grant-burst team-krypton-demo-42 rps=50 duration=6h reason="hackathon demo" approver=eng-oncall`

rate-limit-bot: ACTION: burst_granted for project team-krypton-demo-42. new_concurrency=60 rps (base 10 + burst 50) expires_at=260123...4660. triggered_by=maria.

alex: Verified with Claire — demo resumed, no more 429s. they're seeing smoother responses. :tada:

eng-oncall: Great. Also applied a temporary routing policy that routes to redwood-lite-1.4q for non-critical test endpoints, reduces cost and latency variance.

sam-sales: I'll book a 30-min call with Claire in 48h to discuss Dedicated options and predictable capacity. I'll leave notes on the account.

billing: Logged exception against account: burst_exception (approved_by=eng-oncall, reason=hackathon demo, free_uplift=true). flagged for sales follow-up.

maria: Closing thread: uplift granted until expiry, customer contact claire@teamkrypton.io, billing email billing@teamkrypton.io. Follow-up: sam-sales to own conversion follow-up, eng-oncall to add runbook notes on temporary uplift, billing to file exception.

maria: docs for future: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/support/temporary-bursts and how to run `/grant-burst`.

alex: Thanks everyone — demo finished successfully and they loved the latency. :heart:

maria: leaving a short survey with Claire and asking about next steps. :white_check_mark:
